citation: Van de Sype, L., Vert, M., Sharpanskykh, A., Mohammadi Ziabari, S.S. (2025) Effects of Unplanned Incoming Flights on Airport Relief Processes after a Major Natural Disaster. arXiv:2507.05150

dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of airport relief cargo handling with unplanned incoming flights after a disaster

description: This agent-based model simulates cargo handling at an airport that becomes a relief hub after a major natural disaster, when aid arrives by air and people are evacuated and the airport's sudden capacity need makes it a bottleneck. It was developed by Luka Van de Sype, Matthieu Vert, Alexei Sharpanskykh and Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari at Delft University of Technology and published on arXiv in 2025. Experts identified two main problems, asymmetric information between the airport and incoming flights and a lack of resources; the model therefore implements realistic offloading strategies and resource allocation rules under different degrees of uncertainty about unplanned arrivals. Performance is the average turnaround time, split into offloading, boarding and cumulative waiting times. One unplanned aircraft has negligible effect, but every waiting time grows as more unplanned aircraft arrive. Coverage: a generic relief airport, calibrated and verified with field experts, not on one named event. Access: the arXiv paper only; licence and cost: the paper is CC BY 4.0 and free, and no code release was found. Caveats: no public implementation, stylised airport layout, and results depend on expert-set parameters. It serves emergency response and capacity planning for airports in disasters, and complements the port disruption case studies such as UNCTAD's Port of Houston study catalogued here.
